name: tokens
summary: Writes a Sass map out as CSS custom properties, for any kind of token: colours, spacing, sizes, radii, type, shadows, durations. With the prefix space, (4: 1rem) becomes --space-4: 1rem. A null value is skipped, and a quoted string keeps its quotes.

arguments.name: $map
accepts: a map of names to values, where a value is any CSS value: a colour, a length, a font stack, a shadow, a duration, calc() or clamp()
a value of null, which is skipped
a value that references another token, such as var(--blue-500)
a name without the leading `--`, which the mixin writes itself; an empty value is refused, since a property holding nothing is not one that is unset

arguments.name: $prefix
accepts: null, the default, for no prefix
a name, joined to each property name with a hyphen
a name without a hyphen at either end, since the mixin writes the separator

examples: :root { @include tokens((md: 0 4px 12px rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.08)), shadow); @include tokens((fast: 150ms, ease: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)), motion); }
:root { @include tokens((body: ("Readex Pro", sans-serif), label: "New", focus: null), font); }
caveats: The mixin writes the `--` and, with a prefix, the hyphen after it, so a name or prefix that brings its own doubles them. `(--bg: #fff)` wrote `----bg` and `$prefix: color-` wrote `--color--bg`: real properties in all three engines, holding the value under a name nothing in the stylesheet asks for. Measured in Chrome 152, Firefox 156 and Safari 26.6.2, `----bg` computed to its value while the `--bg` the author would write in `var()` computed to the empty string. Both raise since 4.0.0.

An empty value is not an absence, the same trap as `null`. Measured in all three, `--empty: ;` computed to the empty string and `var(--empty, red)` did not fall back to red. An unquoted empty string and an empty list both raise; a quoted `""` is a real string a `content` can use and is written as it is.
